source_excerpt: (a) The $(i,j)$ entry of $DAD$ is $\varepsilon_i\varepsilon_ja_{ij}$, which equals $a_{ij}$ when $i$ and $j$ lie in the same part and $-a_{ij}$ otherwise. (b) Order the coordinates so that $I$ comes first; then $C=\begin{pmatrix}0&M\\M^T&0\end{pmatrix}$ with $M=A_{I,J}$. Let $M=\sum_k\sigma_ku_kv_k^T$ be a singular value decomposition, with $\sigma_k>0$ and orthonormal families $(u_k)$ and $(v_k)$. The vectors $(u_k,\pm v_k)/\sqrt2$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $C$ with eigenvalues $\pm\sigma_k$. Their orthogonal complement consists of the vectors $(x,y)$ with $x$ orthogonal to the range of $M$ and $y$ orthogonal to the range of $M^T$, that is, with $M^Tx=0$ and $My=0$, and on it $C(x,y)=(My,M^Tx)=0$. Hence the singular values of $C$ are the $\sigma_k$, each counted twice, followed by zeros.

Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:decay}(b): $12.2\cdot2.055<26$.
